newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet crude market murky, cash Brent steadY.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet crude market murky, cash Brent steadY.

text.p: The North Sea physical crude market took on a cloak and dagger air on Thursday with traders reluctant to divulge details of deals done.
At least three cargoes of first decade May Forties were believed to have been traded on the last two days, but players were unwilling to comment.
Differentials were believed to have edged up to Dated Brent +7/+8 cents.
A Norwegian producer said that the sale of an early May Ekofisk on Wednesday was also private and confidential.
The clocking of the two Brent cargoes issued loading dates on Thursday followed two clockings the day before and lent a bearish tone to the wet Brent market.
JP Morgan was clocked with one cargo loading May 2-4, while Mobil was left with the other, which was deferred from May 1-3 loading dates.
"It feels a bit shaky for the next week or so, but on the other hand the general sentiment is not that bearish because the market is generally fairly balanced," said one trader.
CFDs for next week (April 21-25) were a shade weaker, trading at least twice at June Brent -60 cents.

One trader said that these levels, roughly equivalent to May Brent -30 cents, were a fair value of the wet Brent market, but others still pegged the market around May Brent -45 cents, much closer to the last deal done.
"It's so thin it's hard to say, but I think it's unlikely that we're going to get any significant gains on Brent in the near future," a trader said.
Brent intermonth spreads were steady with May/June traded at -30 cents and June/July at -19 cents.
May Brent paper traded at $17.45 and $17.49 a barrel, while June Brent was trading five cents down at $17.76 on the IPE screen at 1737 GMT.
